# Install

How to install pysacd from PyPI, check a download, and build it from source on Linux and macOS.
Windows has its own page: [install on Windows](windows.md).

## From PyPI

Python <!-- facts:python-min -->3.10<!-- /facts --> or later. There are wheels for:

| System | Wheel |
|---|---|
| Linux, glibc 2.28 or later | x86-64 and aarch64 (manylinux) |
| Linux, musl 1.2 or later | x86-64 (musllinux) |
| macOS 11 or later | arm64 (Apple Silicon) |
| macOS 10.13 or later | x86-64 (Intel) |
| Windows | x86-64 |

Anywhere else, pip builds from source ([below](#from-source)). On Windows, follow
[install on Windows](windows.md). The macOS wheels are built for
those versions and run-tested on macOS 15 only (arm64 and x86-64). On macOS 11 to 14 they are
untested, so please report how they do there.

<!-- docs-run: packages=python3-pip expect="^pysacd {version}" -->
```sh
# facts:install kind=pip name=pysacd
pip install pysacd
# /facts
pysacd --version                      # shows how the engine was built
```

The wheel includes the engine, libFLAC and mutagen.

Wheels are portable builds: the PCM filters pick AVX-512, AVX2 or the baseline code when the
library loads.

## Checking a download

The same files are on each [GitHub release](https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd/releases), each
with its build provenance attestation beside it as the wheel's file name plus `.intoto.jsonl`.
Check a wheel with the GitHub CLI (`gh`) against that bundle; no GitHub sign-in is needed. Which
account to name depends on the release.

**Releases up to 0.5.5** were signed before the repository moved to the DSD Toolbox organisation,
so their attestation names `aclater/pysacd`. For 0.5.5's Linux x86-64 wheel:

<!-- docs-run: group=attestation packages=gh -->
<!-- docs-lint: ignore old-owner -- 0.5.5 was signed before the repository moved, so its attestation names aclater/pysacd -->
```sh
# facts:assets repo=dsd-toolbox/pysacd tag=v0.5.5 match="manylinux_2_28_x86_64\.whl" fmt="curl -fsSLO https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd/releases/download/{tag}/{name}"
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd/releases/download/v0.5.5/pysacd-0.5.5-py3-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd/releases/download/v0.5.5/pysacd-0.5.5-py3-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl.intoto.jsonl
# /facts
gh attestation verify pysacd-0.5.5-py3-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl --repo aclater/pysacd \
    --bundle pysacd-0.5.5-py3-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl.intoto.jsonl
```

The command exits 0 when the wheel matches (piped, it prints nothing; in a terminal it may print a success line). Tested on the 0.5.5 wheel
(2026-11-24):

<!-- docs-lint: ignore old-owner -- the table lists what each name gives for the 0.5.5 and earlier releases signed as aclater/pysacd -->
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `--repo aclater/pysacd --bundle` | passes, no sign-in needed |
| `--repo dsd-toolbox/pysacd --bundle` | fails: `verifying with issuer "sigstore.dev"` |
| `--repo aclater/pysacd` (online) | fails: HTTP 404 |
| `--repo dsd-toolbox/pysacd` (online) | fails: HTTP 404 |
| `--owner aclater` (online, signed in with `gh auth login`) | passes |

So for these releases use the bundle form above; the online form works only with
`--owner aclater`, not with `--repo`.

**Releases from 0.6.0** are published and signed from `dsd-toolbox/pysacd`, so they verify with
`--repo dsd-toolbox/pysacd`, with the bundle (as above, names changed to the release's wheel) or
online with `gh auth login` and no `--bundle`. The
[release test plan](../release-test-plan.md) checks both forms on each release.

## From source

On Linux or macOS, the build needs a C compiler and make, and libFLAC for FLAC output. With GCC
before 12 (Ubuntu 22.04's GCC 11, for one) the engine builds without the load-time choice of
AVX-512 or AVX2 for the PCM filters, and they run the baseline code, as the musllinux wheel does
(slower: see [performance](../performance.md), portable builds).

The build downloads the [scarletbook-rs](https://github.com/aclater/scarletbook-rs) C library
that the engine links, from its GitHub release, and checks it against the SHA-256 pinned in
`scarletbook.lock`. To build offline, see
[development](../development.md#the-scarletbook-library).

<!-- docs-run: skip="builds from a source checkout; CI's tests and portability jobs build the same way" -->
```sh
# Fedora/RHEL: sudo dnf install gcc make flac-devel
# Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install gcc make libflac-dev pkg-config
# macOS (Homebrew): brew install flac pkg-config   (clang comes with the Xcode tools)
git clone https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd && cd pysacd
pip install -e '.[convert]'                  # builds a portable engine
make                                         # optional: rebuild it for this CPU
```

`PYSACD_NATIVE=1 pip install .` builds for this CPU from the start.

## Windows

On Windows, install Python from python.org and pysacd with `py -m pip install pysacd` in
PowerShell; no compiler is needed. [Install on Windows](windows.md) has the steps, the first
commands with Windows paths, long paths, and building from source with MSYS2.
